agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Diffusion factors peer evidence and bounded timing implications

analytical_question: What diffusion evidence and factors inform timing for this application and organization without deciding adoption?
general_et_finding: Conservatism does not reduce observed general diffusion: generative-AI work use is substantial and uneven in the defined survey population. Recent D5 movement prevents assuming uninterrupted acceleration. Broad worker-use data still do not identify complete workflow prevalence or a universal adopter category.
application_finding: Relative advantage stays unknown; compatibility stays mixed; complexity remains an inferred technical-review burden; trialability exists only conditionally for approved reversible work; observability needs demonstrable final quality and net effort. A conservative stance changes the required evidence threshold, not these unmeasured population facts.
organization_specific_finding: Only posture changes. This case explicitly requires credible comparable-peer evidence before evaluating a live workflow. It resembles later-adopter behavior conditionally, but laggard or late-majority status cannot be established without relative timing. A trusted technical owner and credible peer demonstrator could help; their actual influence is unverified. Approved source records and training are complements, not proof of diffusion.

evidence.claim: Defined-population work-use data do not measure complete workflow deployment.
evidence.date_or_recency: Published/updated Series updated 2026-10-20 10:40 AM CDT; observed Q2 2026 and Q3 2026; accessed 2026-10-26
evidence.notes: US employed adults aged 18 to 64; RPS nationally representative online labor-market survey | Share reporting generative AI use for their job; quarterly, not seasonally adjusted. | Self report, not installed business workflows; no inference of a durable reversal from one quarter without uncertainty analysis.

evidence.claim: Headline use increased from around 12% to around 35% in that population.
evidence.date_or_recency: Published/updated 2026-07-20; observed Late 2023 to June 2026; June evidence uses BICS Wave 159; accessed 2026-10-26
evidence.evidence_type: Official analysis or original researcher account
evidence.notes: UK BICS businesses; cited headline comparison is businesses with 10 or more employees; excluded industries listed in methods. | Any listed AI technology; the measure does not distinguish light use from embedded production. | All AI, not solely generative AI; UK geography and size threshold do not match the hypothetical US/China team.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Broad external use does not satisfy this organization’s stated reference-evidence requirement.
Absence of peer evidence in the packet does not prove peers are not using the application.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Broad survey signal unchanged; low confidence in matched peer penetration and category assignment.
value_opportunity_implication: Evidence collection may avoid poorly informed timing, at the cost of slower learning.
risk_governance_implication: Retain technical approval and do not label caution technological immaturity.
recommendation_management_implication: Sequence comparable-peer verification and a technical-owner review before considering a live workflow comparison. Preparation using synthetic materials could continue if permitted. Hand the ultimate wait-versus-act decision to the Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: Revisit learning timing when credible peer artifacts meet the stated comparable-context threshold.
Reopen if waiting costs or control capacity change; do not invent their size.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Withhold exact adopter rank and installed-base estimate.
Need independently checkable peer examples with size, geography, workflow and sustained-use dates.
